title: Adaptive Replay Refinement: Allocating Test-Time Compute Between Revision and Resampling
abstract: arXiv:2610.28294v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Test-time scaling allocates additional inference compute to refining existing solutions or generating new ones. This raises a fundamental question: Should I keep improving this solution, or stop working on it and try a completely new solution? Existing methods make this decision using fixed refinement schedules, self-verification judgments, or learned controllers, which can waste compute or rely on signals that may be incorrect or require additional training. We introduce Adaptive Replay Refinement (ARR), a training-free method that detects when a stationary revision reaches a fixed point and reallocates the released compute to a new independent sample; replay decoding treats the current solution as a draft and verifies unchanged tokens in parallel, enabling efficient fixed-point detection. translated_title: 自适应重放优化：在修订与重采样之间分配测试时计算
translated_abstract: 测试时扩展将额外的推理计算用于优化现有解或生成新解。这引出了一个根本性问题：应该继续改进当前解，还是停止改进并尝试一个全新的解？现有方法依赖固定的优化调度、自我验证判断或学习到的控制器来做出这一决策，这可能会浪费计算，或依赖可能不正确、需要额外训练的信号。我们提出自适应重放优化，这是一种无需训练的方法，能够检测平稳修订何时达到不动点，并将释放出来的计算重新分配给新的独立样本；重放解码将当前解视为草稿，并并行验证未发生变化的 token，从而实现高效的不动点检测。在来自五个家族的七个模型和七个基准测试上，ARR 在同等计算量下于五个数学推理基准中的三个上与多数投票的表现相当。
tldr: ARR 是一种无需训练的自适应方法，通过检测解的修订是否达到不动点，在“继续改进现有解”与“重新生成新解”之间动态分配测试时计算，从而在多个模型和基准上以同等计算量达到与多数投票相当的效果。
en_tdlr: ARR is a training-free method that adaptively allocates test-time compute between revising existing solutions and resampling new ones by detecting when refinement reaches a fixed point, matching majority voting performance at equal compute across multiple models and benchmarks.
